references.docstring:
Build a 6x6 pattern by tiling a 2x2 grid, with the middle tile row mirrored left-to-right.

Input structure:
- A 2x2 color tile; no color has a separate background role.

Rule:
- Make a 3-by-3 array of 2x2 tiles.
- Use the input tile unchanged in the top and bottom tile rows.
- Use the left-right mirror of the input tile in the middle tile row.

Key insight:
- The output is not pixel scaling: it is repeated whole-tile placement with a horizontal reflection in the center band.

annotation.src: the entire 2x2 input tile
annotation.dst: the nine 2x2 tile slots in the 6x6 output
annotation.grid_shape: output is 6x6: a 3-by-3 array of 2x2 tiles
annotation.transform: fill the top and bottom tile rows with copies of the original tile; fill the middle tile row with copies of the tile mirrored left-to-right

references.docstring:
Use the small marker glyph as a color code to recolor the larger mask, then erase the marker.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- There are exactly two foreground colors: one larger mask color and one 3x3 marker-glyph color.
- The marker glyph is one of the three 3x3 color-code masks shown by the training examples.
Rule
- Decode the marker glyph: plus -> red, lower-bar glyph -> green, upper-bar glyph with a center gap -> orange.
- Recolor every larger-mask pixel to the decoded color.
- Recolor the marker glyph pixels to the background.
Key insight
- The marker's shape, not its position or color, supplies the replacement color for the larger mask.

annotation.src: large foreground mask plus separate 3x3 marker glyph on the background
annotation.transform: erase the marker glyph; recolor every large-mask pixel to the color decoded from the marker glyph
annotation.symbol_instructions: 3x3 marker glyph maps shape to replacement color: plus -> red, lower-bar glyph -> green, upper-bar glyph with center gap -> orange

references.docstring:
Fill each hollow red square with the size-specific color while preserving its centered red marker.

Input structure
The grid has a black background and red foreground made of one or more
hollow square frames plus one isolated red marker centered inside each frame.

Rule
Copy the input. For every red square frame, recolor all black interior
pixels: 5x5 frames become teal, 7x7 frames become yellow, and 9x9 frames
become green. Red border and marker pixels remain unchanged.

Key insight
The isolated red marker belongs to the hollow frame that contains it, and
the frame side length determines the interior fill color.

annotation.src: red hollow square frames on the black background, each with a centered isolated red marker
annotation.transform: within each frame, recolor all black interior pixels by frame side length: 5x5 -> teal, 7x7 -> yellow, 9x9 -> green; preserve red borders and markers

references.docstring:
Pack the bottom-grounded foreground rectangles into an overlapping diagonal chain starting at the upper-left.

Input structure
The background is the most common color. Every foreground object is a solid
monochrome rectangle touching the bottom row, and the rectangles have unique
left edges that define their left-to-right order.

Rule
Clear the canvas to the background. Copy the rectangles in left-to-right
order, placing the first at the upper-left corner. After placing a rectangle
of height h and width w, place the next rectangle h-1 rows lower and w-1
columns to the right, so later rectangles overwrite the shared corner cell.

Key insight
The bottom arrangement is a horizontal list of rectangles; the output keeps
the list order and rectangle shapes while converting the list into a compact
diagonal chain of overlapping bounding-box corners.

annotation.src: bottom-grounded solid monochrome rectangles s ordered by left edge
annotation.dst: diagonal chain slots d starting at the upper-left; each next slot begins at the previous rectangle's lower-right corner
annotation.match_cond: rank(s by left edge) == rank(d along the chain)
annotation.transform: copy each rectangle into its slot on a background canvas; later rectangles overwrite the shared corner pixel

references.docstring:
Extend each yellow object lane toward the full divider, then continue through the divider side while packing red pixels against the far edge.

Input structure:
- A black grid contains one complete horizontal or vertical divider line.
- Yellow pixels are all on one side of the divider, and red pixels are all on the opposite side.
- Lanes are columns for a horizontal divider and rows for a vertical divider.

Rule:
- Only process lanes that contain yellow pixels.
- Recolor the original yellow pixels green.
- Fill the gap from the nearest yellow pixel to the divider with yellow.
- On the red side of the divider, fill the lane with the divider color and pack the same number of red pixels against the far edge.

Key insight:
- The full divider defines independent one-dimensional lanes; each yellow lane preserves its red count but compresses those red pixels to the far boundary.

annotation.src: yellow pixels in each row/column lane on one side of the full teal divider bar
annotation.path: straight orthogonal path from the nearest yellow pixel to the divider, then along the same lane on the opposite side to the far grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint yellow up to the divider and teal after the divider
annotation.transform: original yellow pixels become green; in each processed lane, keep the input red-pixel count but pack those red pixels against the far edge; lanes without yellow remain unchanged

references.docstring:
Clean a noisy regular array by reconstructing its repeated rectangular sprite and erasing everything outside the slots.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- Non-background cells form a regular grid of solid rectangular sprite slots, plus sparse stray foreground noise.
- Every slot contains a corrupted copy of the same sprite, preserving non-background occupancy.

Rule
- Find the dense row bands and dense column bands of the slot array.
- For each relative position inside the sprite rectangle, take the unique majority color across all slots.
- Fill every slot with that recovered sprite and set all other cells to background.

Key insight
- The intended sprite support is the Cartesian product of dense row bands and dense column bands; noise is too sparse to enter the high-density bands consistently.

annotation.src: regular array of equal-size solid rectangular sprite slots plus sparse foreground noise outside the array; each slot is a corrupted copy of the same sprite
annotation.transform: recover the sprite by unique per-coordinate majority across slots; replace every slot with the recovered sprite and clear all cells outside the slot array to background

references.docstring:
Expand a 3x3 pattern by replacing each colored pixel with a tile shaped like the pattern's black pixels.

Input structure:
- The input is a 3x3 grid with black background cells.
- All non-black pixels share one foreground color.

Rule:
- Treat the black-cell mask of the whole input as a 3x3 tile template.
- For each foreground input pixel, place that tile in the corresponding
  3x3 output block using the foreground color.
- For each black input pixel, leave the corresponding output block black.

Key insight:
- The input is both the coarse placement mask and, by complement, the local
  tile stamped at every foreground position.

annotation.src: 3x3 grid with black cells and one non-black foreground color
annotation.transform: replace each foreground pixel by a 3x3 block whose colored cells are the black-cell positions of the original input; replace each black pixel by an all-black block
annotation.grid_shape: 9x9 block expansion of the 3x3 input

references.docstring:
Connect each same-color pair of marker pixels with a straight segment, drawing vertical segments over horizontal ones.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Each foreground color appears in exactly two marker pixels.
- The two markers of each color share exactly one row or exactly one column.

Rule
- Draw the same-color horizontal or vertical segment between each marker pair, inclusive.
- Paint horizontal segments first, then vertical segments so crossings keep the vertical segment color.

Key insight
- The colored pixels are not isolated objects; same-color pairs are endpoints of axis-aligned segments, and segment orientation determines the crossing layer.

annotation.src: same-color foreground marker pixel pairs on the background
annotation.path: straight row or column segment between the two markers of each color, inclusive
annotation.trajectory: paint every pixel on each segment with the marker-pair color
annotation.transform: keep all other background pixels unchanged
annotation.multi_step: draw horizontal segments first, then vertical segments so vertical-horizontal crossings take the vertical color

references.docstring:
Draw an outward square spiral from the lone marker using the two upper-left palette colors.

Input structure:
- The background is otherwise empty.
- The two non-background pixels at the upper-left are palette controls:
  the left color is for horizontal spiral segments, and the right color is
  for vertical spiral segments.
- The only other foreground pixel is the spiral's center marker, which is
  preserved in the output.

Rule:
- Start at the center marker and walk left, down, right, up, repeating.
- Segment lengths are 2, 3, 4, ... cells.
- Paint horizontal moves with the left palette color and vertical moves with
  the right palette color.
- If the next requested step would leave the grid, stop without painting it.

Key insight:
The corner pixels are not part of the final picture; they encode the colors
of a growing spiral whose geometry is fixed by the marker position and grid
boundary.

annotation.src: single non-palette marker pixel s
annotation.path: from s walk left, down, right, up with segment lengths 2, 3, 4, ...; stop before the first out-of-bounds step
annotation.trajectory: paint each horizontal step with the horizontal palette color and each vertical step with the vertical palette color
annotation.transform: clear the palette pixels; keep s unchanged on the background canvas
annotation.symbol_instructions: upper-left adjacent palette pixels define horizontal color (left) and vertical color (right)

references.docstring:
Recolor each solid interior pixel of a seeded foreground component to that component's marker color.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- A unique majority foreground color forms 4-connected networks of one-cell paths and thick solid blobs.
- Each non-background 4-connected component contains exactly one singleton marker pixel in a non-majority color.

Rule
- For each foreground component, find pixels whose full 3x3 neighborhood lies inside that same component.
- Recolor those 3x3-supported pixels to the component's marker color.
- Leave background, one-cell paths, and blob borders unchanged.

Key insight
- Thick blob interiors are exactly the component pixels with all eight neighbors present; corridors and borders fail this local 3x3 test.

annotation.src: 4-connected foreground networks of one-cell paths and thick solid blobs; each network has one singleton non-majority marker color
annotation.transform: within each network, recolor every foreground pixel whose full 3x3 neighborhood stays inside that network to the marker color; preserve paths, blob borders, and background

references.docstring:
Collapse the lattice of filled rectangular objects into a compact color grid.

Input structure
- The input has a dominant background with scattered clutter colors.
- The meaningful objects are monochromatic 4-connected foreground rectangles, each at least 3x3 and exactly filling its bbox.
- These rectangles form a complete lattice whose same-row and same-column bbox intervals overlap.

Rule
- Keep only the filled rectangular objects.
- Group their vertical bbox intervals into output rows and their horizontal bbox intervals into output columns.
- Fill each compact output cell with the color of the rectangle at the corresponding lattice position.

Key insight
- The clutter is not a filled 3x3-or-larger rectangle; the rectangles' overlapping bbox bands define the small table axes.

annotation.src: 4-connected monochrome filled rectangular foreground objects embedded among scattered clutter
annotation.transform: collapse each rectangle to one pixel of its color, preserving the rectangle-lattice row and column positions and discarding clutter
annotation.grid_shape: number of overlapping rectangle row bands x number of overlapping rectangle column bands

references.docstring:
Recolor each teal object by how many enclosed black holes it contains.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one or more 4-connected teal objects.
- Each teal object encloses one to four 4-connected black regions inside its bbox.

Rule
- Count the enclosed black regions for each teal object.
- Recolor the object's pixels: one hole -> blue, two holes -> green, three holes -> red, four holes -> yellow.
- Leave the black background unchanged.

Key insight
- The varied object shapes and sizes are distractions; the color class is determined by topological hole count.

annotation.src: 4-connected teal foreground objects on a black background
annotation.transform: for each object, count its enclosed 4-connected black hole regions and recolor all object pixels by that count: 1 hole -> blue, 2 -> green, 3 -> red, 4 -> yellow; preserve black bg

references.docstring:
Continue the equally spaced marker line past its last blue marker, painting the continuation red.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color.
- Exactly one foreground color marks three pixels on a straight arithmetic line.
- The three marker pixels are equally spaced.

Rule
- Order the markers along the line in row-major direction.
- Use the vector between consecutive markers as the step.
- Starting one step beyond the last marker, paint each in-bounds background cell red.
- Stop before the next step would leave the grid.

Key insight
- The three blue pixels are not copied; they define the spacing and direction of a line continuation.

annotation.src: three same-color marker pixels on the background
annotation.path: order the markers along their equally spaced straight line; continue from the last marker by the same vector until the next step would leave the grid
annotation.trajectory: paint each visited background pixel red
annotation.transform: keep the original markers and all other cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Crop the four sprites separated by a solid cross and pack them into a 2x2 montage.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One non-background color forms a full solid row and a full solid column,
  splitting the grid into four nonempty quadrants.
- Each quadrant contains exactly one single-color sprite on the background;
  each sprite has a 3x3 tight bounding box.

Rule
- Remove the separator row and column.
- In each quadrant, crop the sprite to its tight bounding box, preserving
  background holes inside the crop.
- Concatenate the four crops in quadrant order: upper-left, upper-right,
  lower-left, lower-right.

Key insight
- The cross is only a layout divider; the output is a compact atlas of the
  four local sprites in their original relative quadrant positions.

annotation.src: grid divided into four regions by a solid one-pixel separator cross, with one 3x3-bbox sprite in each region
annotation.transform: remove the separator cross; crop each sprite to its tight bbox and concatenate the crops in upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right quadrant order
annotation.grid_shape: 6x6 montage of four 3x3 sprite crops

references.docstring:
Swap each non-legend foreground color with its row-mate in the 2x2 upper-left legend.

Input structure
- A dominant background separates a full 2x2 foreground legend in the
  upper-left corner from the main multicolor foreground object.
- The main object uses exactly the four colors shown in the legend.

Rule
- Leave the legend and background unchanged.
- Treat each legend row as a bidirectional color pair.
- Recolor every foreground pixel outside the legend to the other color in
  its legend row, using the original input colors for a simultaneous swap.

Key insight
- The small 2x2 block is a symbol instruction, not part of the object: its
  rows define the pairwise color substitutions for the separate object.

annotation.summary: Use the 2x2 upper-left legend as two row-wise color swaps for the separate foreground object.
annotation.src: foreground pixels outside the upper-left 2x2 legend
annotation.transform: simultaneously replace each target pixel color with the other color in its legend row; keep the legend and background unchanged
annotation.symbol_instructions: the 2x2 legend pairs the two colors in each row as a bidirectional substitution

references.docstring:
Build a double-sized mirror mosaic with the original grid in the lower-right quadrant.

Input structure
- A rectangular 2D color grid.

Rule
- Place the original grid in the lower-right quadrant of the output.
- Fill the lower-left quadrant with a left-right reflection of the input.
- Fill the upper-right quadrant with an up-down reflection of the input.
- Fill the upper-left quadrant with the 180-degree rotation of the input.

Key insight
- The output is a mirrored extension of the input upward and left, not a pixel-scale zoom.

annotation.src: entire input grid used as the lower-right quadrant seed
annotation.dst: 2x2 grid of input-size quadrants
annotation.transform: fill quadrants by reflecting the seed across the new center axes: upper-left 180 degrees, upper-right up-down reflection, lower-left left-right reflection, lower-right unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 2

references.docstring:
Combine the two stacked masks by marking the cells that are empty in both panels.

Input structure:
- The input is a 2D grid with black background.
- A single solid non-background row uses a color that appears only in that row.
- That separator row splits the grid into two nonempty same-size panels, each with one foreground color.

Rule:
- Remove the separator row and align the top and bottom panels by position.
- Output a black grid with the panel shape.
- Paint a teal pixel at each position where both aligned panel pixels are black.

Key insight:
- The output is the intersection of the two panels' background masks, not a combination of their foreground shapes.

annotation.src: two same-size foreground/background panels separated by a unique solid row
annotation.transform: remove the separator and replace each aligned pixel pair with teal iff both source pixels are background, otherwise black
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one panel

references.docstring:
Complete blue guide lines from border marker pairs and recolor every red object touched by the completed lines.

Input structure
- The grid has one background color, one sparse singleton marker color, and one object color.
- Marker pixels on matching left/right borders define horizontal guide rows; marker pixels on matching top/bottom borders define vertical guide columns.

Rule
- Draw each guide row or column across the whole grid in the marker color.
- Any 4-connected object-color component that overlaps or 4-neighbor touches a completed guide line is recolored entirely to the marker color.

Key insight
- The border markers are not objects to move; they are controls for guide lines whose contact with object components selects the objects to recolor.

annotation.src: singleton marker pixels on opposite grid borders
annotation.path: matching left/right border markers emit a full horizontal row; matching top/bottom border markers emit a full vertical column
annotation.trajectory: paint the entire guide row or column with the marker color
annotation.transform: recolor every 4-connected object-color object that overlaps or 4-neighbor touches a completed guide line to the marker color; preserve the other objects

references.docstring:
Draw a grey orthogonal route from the red marker to the yellow marker and then from the yellow marker to the green marker.

Input structure
- A black-background grid containing exactly one red pixel, one yellow pixel, and one green pixel.
- The marker pixels are the only foreground cells in the input.

Rule
- Preserve the three colored marker pixels.
- For red-to-yellow and yellow-to-green, draw the connecting path by moving horizontally to the target column, then vertically to the target row.
- Paint only background cells along those paths grey.

Key insight
- The yellow marker is the bend waypoint between the red start and green finish; each hop uses the same horizontal-first Manhattan routing.

annotation.src: red marker pixel, with yellow marker as waypoint and green marker as final target
annotation.path: from red to yellow, then from yellow to green; each leg moves horizontally to the target column before moving vertically to the target row
annotation.trajectory: paint every background pixel on the two orthogonal route legs grey
annotation.transform: preserve the red, yellow, and green marker pixels

references.docstring:
Expand each colored marker into a full-width horizontal band frame determined by marker-row proximity.

Input structure
- A 2D grid with a dominant background color.
- The foreground consists of isolated one-pixel colored markers.
- Marker rows are unique; marker columns only identify the original pixel and do not affect the frame width.

Rule
- Sort markers by row and split the grid into horizontal bands at the midpoint between consecutive marker rows.
- For each marker's band, paint the left and right boundary columns with the marker color.
- Paint the marker's own row across the full width; also paint the top or bottom grid edge when the band touches it.

Key insight
- The single pixels are row anchors for full-width frames: each color owns the rows vertically closest to its marker.

annotation.src: singleton foreground marker pixels on the background, with unique marker rows
annotation.transform: split the grid into horizontal bands at row midpoints between adjacent markers; in each band paint the side columns, the marker row, and any touched top or bottom grid edge with the marker color

references.docstring:
Recolor the enlarged mask with the small colored template rotated 90 degrees clockwise.

Input structure
- A background grid contains one small multicolor template and one much larger monochrome mask.
- The monochrome mask is an integer block scale of the template foreground mask after a 90-degree clockwise rotation.

Rule
- Rotate the template bbox 90 degrees clockwise, scale each template pixel to the matching block size, and use that scaled template to recolor the large mask pixels.
- Preserve the original template and all background pixels.

Key insight
- The large mask gives only the silhouette; the small template supplies the colors once it is rotated and scaled to that silhouette.

annotation.src: small colored template region s
annotation.dst: large monochrome mask region d
annotation.match_cond: d.mask == block-scaled 90-degree-clockwise rotation of s.foreground_mask
annotation.transform: replace each mask-color pixel in d with the corresponding color from the rotated, block-scaled s; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Add a one-step inward miniature of the three colored square-corner markers plus a grey center pixel.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Exactly three non-background pixels appear at three corners of one axis-aligned square.
- The square has an integer center and enough span that the inward miniature is separate from the original markers.

Rule:
- Keep the input unchanged.
- Paint the square center grey.
- For each colored corner marker, paint the pixel one diagonal step from the center toward that marker with the marker's color.

Key insight:
The three markers define both the missing fourth corner and the square center; the output draws a scaled-down copy of the observed corner pattern around that center.

annotation.src: three single-pixel foreground markers occupying three corners of an axis-aligned square
annotation.transform: preserve the markers, paint grey at the square center, and copy each marker color to the cell one diagonal step from the center toward that marker

references.docstring:
Continue the grey-bracketed top motif downward through the empty suffix.

Input structure
The grid has a black background. A contiguous run of grey pixels begins at
the top of the leftmost column; those grey pixels mark the rows of a colored
motif. Below the marked rows there may be other foreground rows, followed by
an all-background suffix.

Rule
Copy the marked rows as a motif after changing the grey marker cells to
background. Starting just below the lowest existing foreground row, write
those motif rows cyclically into the empty suffix, preserving the original
grid everywhere else.

Key insight
The grey segment is a bracket for the motif height; the fill below the
existing drawing restarts from the first marked row rather than continuing
from any unmarked foreground row.

annotation.summary: Extend the grey-marked top motif downward through the empty bottom rows.
annotation.src: top row motif marked by a contiguous grey run in the leftmost column, with the grey marker cells excluded
annotation.dst: empty suffix rows below the lowest existing foreground row
annotation.transform: repeat the marked motif rows cyclically from the first marked row into the suffix; preserve all existing pixels elsewhere

references.docstring:
Stamp recolored copies of the foreground template in the order given by the marker pixels.

Input structure
- A dominant background contains one multi-pixel foreground template color.
- Every other foreground color is a single marker pixel.
- The marker pixels lie on one common row or one common column.

Rule
- Crop the template color to its bounding box and use it as a mask.
- Sort markers left-to-right when they share a row, or top-to-bottom when they share a column.
- For each sorted marker, make one copy of the template mask recolored to that marker color.
- Concatenate the copies horizontally for a marker row, or vertically for a marker column.

Key insight
- The single pixels are an ordered palette; the larger foreground shape is a reusable stencil.

annotation.src: singleton marker pixels s ordered left-to-right when they share a row, or top-to-bottom when they share a column; plus the multi-pixel foreground template mask
annotation.dst: consecutive template-sized output slots d along the same row/column axis
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: crop the template bbox; in each d stamp the template mask recolored to s.color, leaving non-mask cells as background
annotation.grid_shape: template bbox height by template bbox width times marker count; axis follows the marker row/column

references.docstring:
Recolor each small monochromatic foreground object green while leaving larger objects unchanged.

Input structure
- The dominant color is the background.
- The foreground is split into monochromatic 4-connected objects of several colors.
- Green is absent from the input and is the output marker color.

Rule
- Find every non-background same-color 4-connected object.
- If an object's area is one or two pixels, recolor all of its pixels green.
- Keep objects with area at least three unchanged.

Key insight
The selected pixels are the complete small color-components, independent of their color or position.

annotation.src: monochromatic 4-connected foreground objects on the background
annotation.transform: recolor each object of area one or two pixels green; preserve objects of area at least three and the background

references.docstring:
Extend every colored segment straight toward the single solid edge bar, with nearer segments covering farther projections.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Exactly one full grid edge is a solid non-background bar.
- All other foreground objects are 4-connected, monochrome, one-cell-thick segments parallel to that edge.

Rule
- Each segment paints the rectangular strip from itself to the cell before the edge bar, perpendicular to the segment.
- Strips farther from the edge bar are painted first; closer strips overwrite them wherever their rectangular regions overlap.
- The original edge bar remains unchanged.

Key insight
- The edge bar acts as the direction cue and occluding wall: every segment casts a same-color projection toward it, and distance to the wall determines visible layering.

annotation.src: non-wall colored one-cell-thick segments parallel to the single full-edge bar
annotation.path: orthogonal strip from each segment toward the full-edge bar, stopping at the cell before the bar
annotation.trajectory: paint the whole segment-width rectangular strip with the segment color
annotation.transform: keep the full-edge bar unchanged
annotation.multi_step: paint farther-from-bar strips before nearer-to-bar strips so nearer projections cover overlaps

references.docstring:
Paint the empty gutters of a rectangular lattice of grey 2x2 blocks.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- The only foreground color forms a complete rectangular array of separated 2x2 blocks.
- Blank row bands and column bands between adjacent block bands are the lattice gutters.

Rule:
- Keep the grey blocks unchanged.
- Paint gutter background pixels red inside the foreground bounding rectangle.
- Paint gutter background pixels blue where the same gutter rows or columns extend outside that bounding rectangle.

Key insight:
- The grey blocks define row bands and column bands; their intervening blank bands are the lines to color, and the block-array bbox separates internal gutters from exterior extensions.

annotation.summary: Empty gutters between grey block rows and columns are colored red inside the block-array bbox and blue on exterior extensions.
annotation.src: grey 2x2 block lattice on the background; blank row/column bands between adjacent block bands are gutters
annotation.transform: paint background pixels in gutter rows/columns red inside the lattice bbox and blue where those same gutter rows/columns extend outside the bbox

references.docstring:
Turn each blue control pixel into a red-centered cross with green diagonal corner marks.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color and one foreground color.
- The foreground pixels are blue control pixels.
- The output has the same shape as the input.

Rule:
- Paint the full row and full column through every blue control pixel blue.
- Paint the four in-bounds diagonal neighbors of each control pixel green.
- Recolor each original control pixel red.

Key insight:
- The sparse blue pixels are centers of identical local-and-global marks: global
  row/column rays plus a local diagonal-neighbor decoration.

annotation.src: blue control pixels s on the dominant background
annotation.path: from each s, straight horizontal and vertical rays to the grid boundaries along s.row and s.column
annotation.trajectory: paint blue continuously along each ray
annotation.transform: recolor each s pixel red; paint each in-bounds diagonal neighbor of s green; leave all other cells as background

references.docstring:
Complete each yellow-marked plus motif by recoloring its grey cells red.

Input structure
- The grid contains black empty cells plus grey and yellow foreground cells.
- Each 8-connected yellow object is a subset of one clipped five-cell plus
  made from yellow and grey cells.

Rule
- For every 8-connected yellow object, find the unique plus center whose
  in-bounds center/up/down/left/right cells contain the yellow object and no
  black cells.
- Recolor the grey cells of that plus red; keep yellow and black cells fixed.

Key insight
- The yellow pixels are partial cross markers, and the surrounding grey cells
  in the same cross are the missing cells to highlight.

annotation.src: 8-connected yellow marker objects embedded in grey/yellow clipped plus motifs on black background
annotation.transform: for each marker object, find the unique center/up/down/left/right plus containing it and recolor the grey cells of that plus red; preserve black and yellow cells

references.docstring:
Recolor the blue pixels matching the accent-coded 3x3 mask inside every qualifying lattice cell.

Input structure
- The grid is a lattice of 3x3 cells separated by yellow lines.
- One non-blue, non-yellow accent color appears only as 2x2 blocks inside a 6x6 instruction region.
- Ordinary candidate cells contain only empty and blue pixels.

Rule
- Decode the instruction region into a 3x3 mask: each solid 2x2 accent block marks the corresponding mask pixel.
- For every 3x3 lattice cell containing blue pixels at all mask positions, recolor those mask-position pixels to the accent color.
- Preserve the instruction region, yellow lattice, empty pixels, and all non-matching blue pixels.

Key insight
- The accent shape is a scaled-up code for which positions in a 3x3 blue pattern should be recolored.

annotation.src: 3x3 blue/background lattice cells plus one 6x6 accent instruction region
annotation.transform: decode the instruction as a 3x3 mask; in every 3x3 cell where all mask positions are blue, recolor those positions to the accent color and leave other pixels unchanged
annotation.symbol_instructions: each solid 2x2 accent block in the 6x6 instruction region marks the corresponding pixel of the 3x3 mask

references.docstring:
Recolor each closed orthogonal line loop so convex bend pixels are yellow and concave bend pixels are red.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background and exactly one foreground color.
- The foreground forms one or more 4-connected one-pixel-wide closed cycles; every foreground pixel has degree 2.
Rule
- Trace each cycle and inspect the turn at each foreground pixel.
- Straight pixels keep the original foreground color.
- Bend pixels whose turn direction is the majority direction for that cycle are convex corners and become yellow.
- Bend pixels whose turn direction is the minority direction for that cycle are concave corners and become red.
Key insight
- A simple rectilinear closed boundary has exactly four more convex bends than concave bends, so convexity can be inferred structurally from the majority turn sign within each traced cycle.

annotation.src: monochrome one-cell-wide 4-connected closed orthogonal cycles on the background

references.docstring:
Fill each bottom-marked vertical column by propagating the next colored pixel below upward through background cells.

references.docstring:
Complete each framed motif by reflecting it to the opposite side of its frame.

Input structure

Rule
- Infer the frame color as the unique non-background color with the largest

- The frame's aspect ratio identifies the symmetry direction, and the output is

- Detect the enclosed background holes inside the large objects.

references.docstring:
Return the color of the unique topmost bar in a stack of overlaid horizontal and vertical bars.

Input structure:

Rule:
- Reconstruct each foreground color as a full-height or full-width bar from

- At every horizontal/vertical crossing, add a lower-to-higher constraint
  toward the visible color.

Key insight:
- The answer is not the largest or most frequent bar; the crossings encode a

references.docstring:
Extract the contents enclosed by the largest complete rectangular frame.

Input structure
- The grid is mostly background noise plus several monochrome rectangular frames.
- Each frame has a one-pixel-thick border; the interior may contain any colors.

- Find all complete same-color rectangular frame borders.

- The frame border is only a locator; the desired output is the raw enclosed region of the largest frame.

references.docstring:

- The blue structure's bbox is a three-row band whose internal black components form candidate cavities.

- The pockets are the black 4-connected components inside the blue bbox that touch the bbox's bottom edge.

- Matching is by fitting a whole lower cavity, not by the gray object's current position; extra cells may stick out only through surrounding black space.

references.docstring:
Replace grey rectangles indicated by three same-color corner markers with that marker color.

references.docstring:

- The task is not about the connected teal objects globally; it is a local

references.docstring:
Bend the single foreground lattice into a one-pixel horizontal wave anchored at its bottom row.

- Keep the bottom row of the object's bounding box fixed.

- The phase of the wave is determined from the bottom of the object, not from the top.

references.docstring:

Input structure:

- Ignore black pixels while inferring the repeating tile.

- Black is missing data, not part of the wallpaper; the observed colored cells determine the latent periodic tile.

annotation.src: non-black cells of a periodic wallpaper with black holes

references.docstring:
Extend the eight non-center cells of a filled 3x3 block as rays to the grid edge.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- All foreground pixels form exactly one filled 3x3 block.
- The middle cell of that block is the center, and the other eight cells are compass-direction ray seeds.

- Keep the input grid unchanged as the base output.
- For each non-center cell in the 3x3 block, continue its color away from the center in that cell's compass direction.

- The local position of a cell around the 3x3 center is also its global ray direction.

annotation.trajectory: paint every traversed pixel with the source pixel color

references.docstring:
Recolor each placeholder object by the control pixel at the matching relative position inside the legend.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- A large single-color legend body forms a rectangle containing one-pixel

- Outside the legend rectangle, all foreground pixels have one placeholder
  color and form the same number of 8-connected objects as there are markers.

Rule:
- Treat the bbox of all placeholder objects as a map of their layout.
- Treat the legend bbox as the corresponding map of control-pixel positions.
- Match placeholder objects to markers by the unique minimum total distance
  between bbox-center relative positions.
- Recolor every pixel of each placeholder object with its matched marker

- The gray block is a positional legend: marker locations, not marker color

annotation.dst: colored control pixels d inside the grey legend rectangle
annotation.match_cond: s.bbox_center relative position in the placeholder-object bbox matches d.position relative to the legend bbox

annotation.symbol_instructions: grey legend rectangle encodes the target color for each outside object by relative marker position

references.docstring:
Erase every pixel whose color matches the marker inside the corner bracket, except for the marker itself.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- There is exactly one monochromatic 4-connected corner bracket object.
- Inside the bracket bbox, outside the bracket cells, there is exactly one foreground marker pixel.
Rule
- Read the marker color.
- Recolor every other pixel of that color to the background.
- Leave the bracket, the marker, and all other colors unchanged.
Key insight
- The bracket is a color selector: its enclosed marker names the color to delete everywhere else.

annotation.src: unique monochrome L-shaped corner bracket containing one non-background marker pixel; all pixels sharing the marker color

references.docstring:

Input structure:

- The visible non-blank pixels follow a repeated color cycle by column.
- Cells on or above the main diagonal use the column's cycle phase; cells
  below the diagonal use the next cycle phase.

Rule:
- Infer the unique blank color and the ordered color cycle from all visible
  pixels.
- Reconstruct the complete table with phase col mod n above/on the diagonal
  and phase col+1 mod n below it.
- Replace only blank pixels with their reconstructed colors.

Key insight:
- The apparent holes are not independent objects; they are missing samples
  from one global periodic pattern with a diagonal phase shift.

annotation.dst: blank pixels of the same table
annotation.transform: infer the ordered column color cycle; fill each blank with cycle[col mod n] on or above the main diagonal, and cycle[(col+1) mod n] below the diagonal

references.docstring:

- The black background contains exactly two 4-connected multicolor foreground objects.

- One object is complete; the other is a damaged copy with only foreground cells removed.

- Align the two object crops by their bbox top-left corners.

- Crop that missing-cell mask to its own bbox, recolor selected cells teal, and leave other cells black.

Key insight
- The output is not one of the colored motifs; it is the shape of the damage after subtracting the smaller motif mask from the larger matching motif mask.

annotation.dst: damaged same-sized motif object d
annotation.match_cond: s.bbox.shape == d.bbox.shape; overlapping foreground pixels have the same colors and d.mask is a strict subset of s.mask
annotation.transform: emit the tight crop of s.mask - d.mask as teal pixels on black
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop of the missing-cell mask

references.docstring:
Expand each input pixel to a 2x2 block, replacing every grey pixel with a blue/red checkerboard block.

Key insight
The output is a fixed local rewrite of each input pixel, not a movement or global pattern completion.

annotation.transform: rewrite each black pixel as a black 2x2 block and each grey pixel as a blue/red checkerboard 2x2 block

references.docstring:
Stack the colored rectangles by size after aligning their upper-left corners.

- The input positions only reveal each rectangle's size; the output re-stacks the same rectangles at a common origin.

annotation.dst: same-origin output layers d ordered back-to-front by decreasing area

references.docstring:

- The markers define identical cells; the sprite's shape matters, but its off-center position inside the cell is normalized to the cell center.

references.docstring:
Recolor every third monochromatic foreground bar in top-to-bottom order red, starting with the first.

- The selected objects are not chosen by their color or size; only their ordinal position in the vertical object sequence matters.

annotation.transform: recolor ranks 1, 4, 7, ... to red and leave the other objects unchanged

references.docstring:

The hidden objects are the only large uniform rectangular regions; maximality

- Split the grid at the divider rows and columns.

annotation.symbol_instructions: marker run length gives both the code-row frequency to select and the bar height
