- Marker pixels are isolated enough that their four-neighbor stamps do not overlap or touch another marker.

Rule
- Keep every original blue marker pixel unchanged.
- For each marker, recolor its in-bounds background neighbor above to red, left to orange, right to pink, and below to teal.
- Clip the stamp at the grid boundary.

Key insight
- The marker position is an anchor; the added color is determined solely by compass direction from that anchor.

annotation.src: isolated blue marker pixels on a black background
annotation.transform: preserve each marker; paint each in-bounds background neighbor by direction: above -> red, left -> orange, right -> pink, below -> teal

references.docstring:
Recolor every second grey marker from the right edge to green.

Input structure
The grid has three rows, black background, and exactly one grey foreground
pixel in each column.

Rule
Starting with the rightmost column, recolor the grey foreground pixel in
every other column to green; leave the skipped grey pixels and background
unchanged.

Key insight
The foreground pixels form a left-to-right sequence, and the output marks
alternating sequence positions counted from the right.

annotation.src: grey marker pixels s, one per column, ordered right-to-left by column
annotation.dst: same marker locations
annotation.transform: recolor the 1st, 3rd, 5th, ... markers in that order to green; leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Extend every colored marker that is row- or column-aligned with the 2x2 anchor square until it touches that square.

Input structure
- The background contains one non-background 2x2 square anchor.
- All other foreground objects are single colored marker pixels.
- Some marker pixels share one row or one column with the anchor square.

Rule
- Keep the anchor and all original marker pixels unchanged.
- For each marker on an anchor row, paint horizontally from the marker to the cell next to the anchor.
- For each marker on an anchor column, paint vertically from the marker to the cell next to the anchor.
- Ignore markers that are not aligned with any anchor row or column.

Key insight
- The 2x2 square supplies the only two active rows and two active columns; aligned singleton markers emit straight segments into the nearest side of the square.

annotation.src: single colored marker pixels that share a row or column with the 2x2 foreground anchor square
annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical segment from each aligned marker along the shared row/column to the cell adjacent to the anchor
annotation.dst: nearest side of the 2x2 anchor square
annotation.trajectory: paint every background pixel on the segment with the marker color
annotation.transform: keep the anchor square and all original marker pixels unchanged; ignore unaligned markers

references.docstring:
Replace the noisy 5x5 single-color mask with the fixed 3x3 grey symbol encoded by its foreground color.

Input structure:
- The input is a 5x5 grid with black background.
- All foreground pixels share one visible color: red, blue, or green.
- The exact foreground pixel positions vary within each color class.

Rule:
- Red emits a grey top-T symbol.
- Blue emits a grey plus symbol.
- Green emits a grey lower-right L symbol.
- The output background is black and the symbol pixels are grey.

Key insight:
- The foreground shape is distractor noise; the single foreground color is the code for the 3x3 output symbol.

annotation.src: 5x5 black-background mask with exactly one foreground color
annotation.transform: ignore foreground positions and replace the grid with the grey symbol encoded by that color: red -> top-T, blue -> plus, green -> lower-right L

references.docstring:
Connect a red pixel to a teal pixel with a yellow right-angle path.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background with exactly one red pixel and one teal pixel.
- The red and teal pixels are not in the same row or column.
- The output keeps the original endpoint pixels.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Draw yellow horizontally from the red pixel's row to the teal pixel's column.
- Draw yellow vertically along the teal pixel's column until reaching the teal pixel.

Key insight:
- The teal pixel supplies the destination column first, so the path is an L shape
  with its corner aligned to the red row and teal column.

Fill the inside of a cup and extend teal outward through its opening.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one non-black cup-shaped object on a black background.
- The cup is an almost closed rectangular outline with one boundary opening.
- Black cells inside the cup and at the opening define the fill and exit path.

Rule:
- Find the cup's bounding box and mark the black cells inside it.
- Fill those interior cells with teal.
- Detect the opening side and draw teal straight outward from every opening cell.

Key insight:
- The only boundary gap identifies both the cup interior and the direction for the
  emitted teal line.

Swap every teal pixel with gray and every gray pixel with teal.

Input structure:
- The input is an arbitrary square grid of non-black colors.
- Teal and gray may appear anywhere in the grid.
- Other colors are not part of the swap.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Recolor original gray cells to teal.
- Recolor original teal cells to gray while leaving all other cells unchanged.

Key insight:
- The transformation is a pure color substitution, so positions and all non-target
  colors are preserved exactly.

Erase the red rectangular outlines and recolor each enclosed black interior green.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one foreground color, red.
- Red foreground components are 4-connected axis-aligned rectangles.
- A component is either a one-cell-thick hollow rectangular frame or a solid rectangle with no black interior.

Rule
- Start from an all-background output grid of the same shape.
- For each hollow red rectangular frame, fill its strict bbox interior with green.
- Solid red rectangles and all red frame borders are erased to background.

Key insight
- The red pixels only mark rectangular boundaries; the retained output is the background region enclosed by each boundary, recolored green.

annotation.src: red 4-connected hollow rectangular frames and solid red rectangles on a black background
annotation.transform: erase all red pixels; for each hollow frame, recolor its enclosed black bbox interior green; solid rectangles contribute nothing

references.docstring:
Summarize the non-black pixels as one horizontal row of their color.

Input structure
The input is a grid with black background and exactly one foreground color
appearing in one or more pixels.
Rule
Count the non-black pixels and return a 1 x count row filled with the
foreground color.
Key insight
The positions of the foreground pixels are irrelevant; only their color and
population determine the compact output.

annotation.src: single non-black foreground color mask on black background
annotation.transform: count the foreground pixels and emit that many pixels of the foreground color in one horizontal row
annotation.grid_shape: 1 x foreground pixel count

references.docstring:
Move each interior marker to the cell just inside the matching-color frame side.

Input structure
The grid has background-colored corners, a one-cell rectangular frame, and a
background interior containing colored marker pixels.

Rule
Clear the frame interior. If an interior marker has the top, bottom, left, or
right frame-side color, repaint it just inside that side while preserving its
original column or row. Interior colors not used by any frame side disappear.

Key insight
The four side colors are directional labels, so each marker's color selects
the target side and its orthogonal coordinate supplies the placement.

annotation.src: colored marker pixel s inside the rectangular frame
annotation.dst: inner-edge slot d adjacent to a frame side
annotation.match_cond: s.color equals d's frame-side color; top/bottom slots keep s.column and left/right slots keep s.row
annotation.transform: clear the frame interior to bg; paint matched markers at d and delete marker colors absent from the frame

references.docstring:
Connect two separated rectangles by coloring the gap between them teal.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background with two monochromatic rectangle objects.
- The rectangles are separated by at least a small black gap.
- Teal is reserved for the connecting bridge.

Rule:
- Detect the two non-black connected components.
- Scan black cells and test which ones lie between the two rectangles.
- Recolor those between-object cells teal.

Key insight:
- The bridge is not drawn from a fixed endpoint; it is the set of background cells
  geometrically between the two object footprints.

Fill the 2x2 marker block with the singleton colors found in matching surrounding quadrants.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background, one solid 2x2 foreground marker block, and four other foreground singleton pixels.
- Each singleton lies diagonally outside the marker block: above/below it and left/right of it.

Rule
- Clear all foreground pixels from the canvas.
- Place each singleton color into the cell of the marker block in the same relative quadrant: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, or lower-right.

Key insight
- The 2x2 block is a compact target window; each scattered singleton's side relative to that block determines its destination cell.

annotation.src: colored singleton pixel s outside the solid 2x2 marker block
annotation.dst: cell d of the marker block
annotation.match_cond: s and d occupy the same relative quadrant around the marker block: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, or lower-right
annotation.transform: clear all original foreground pixels; write each singleton color into its matched marker-block cell

references.docstring:
Complete the partially shown horizontal motif by repeating its minimal column period across the grid.

Input structure
The input is a rectangular grid with a dominant background color and a
foreground motif drawn from the left edge across part of the rows.

Rule
Find the smallest column period for which all visible foreground pixels agree
by row and column residue, then repeat that period across the full width.

Key insight
The background cells to the right are not empty final cells; they are the
missing later copies of the same minimal horizontal tile already visible at
the left.

annotation.src: left-edge prefix of a horizontal periodic foreground motif on the background
annotation.dst: missing right-side suffix columns of the same full-width grid
annotation.transform: infer the minimal column period consistent with all visible foreground pixels by row and column residue, then repeat that tile across the full width

references.docstring:
Recolor every red-green domino to a teal pixel at the green cell and erase the red cell.

Input structure
- The grid is a black-background scene containing red pixels, green pixels, and grey marker pixels.
- Some red and green pixels form isolated 4-connected two-cell dominoes; other red/green pixels are unpaired distractors.
Rule
- For each 4-connected red-green domino, set the green pixel to teal and set the red pixel to the background color.
- Preserve grey pixels and all unpaired red/green pixels.
Key insight
- Only orthogonal red-green contact matters: the green side survives as the new teal marker while the red side is deleted.

annotation.src: 4-connected red-green dominoes on a black background, with grey markers and unpaired red/green pixels preserved
annotation.transform: recolor each domino's green pixel to teal and recolor its red pixel to bg

references.docstring:
Grow red paths upward from red starts while sidestepping gray obstacles to the right.

Input structure:
- The grid has red start pixels along the bottom row.
- Gray pixels are scattered as obstacles away from the outer border.
- All other cells are black background.

Rule:
- For each red start, attempt to move one cell upward at each step.
- If the cell above is gray, draw one red step to the right instead.
- Stop a path when it reaches the top or can no longer sidestep within the grid.

Key insight:
- Each path follows a simple local rule: upward progress is preferred, and gray
  blockers only cause rightward detours.

Extract the color enclosed by the unique 3x3 monochrome frame and return it as a 1x1 grid.

Input structure
- A background canvas contains scattered foreground pixels in two visible colors.
- Exactly one 3x3 window has all eight border pixels in one foreground color and its center in a different foreground color.

Rule
- Find that window and output a 1x1 grid containing the center pixel color.

Key insight
- The complete 3x3 frame marks the meaningful sample; the scattered pixels of the same colors are distractors.

annotation.src: scattered two-color foreground pixels with one complete 3x3 monochrome frame around a different-colored center pixel
annotation.transform: replace the grid with the color of the center pixel enclosed by the complete 3x3 frame
annotation.grid_shape: 1x1 label cell

references.docstring:
Overlay the two side-by-side foreground masks and render their union in pink.

Input structure
The input is two equal square panels placed horizontally on a black
background. Each panel contains exactly one non-background foreground color,
and the two panel colors are different. Pink is absent from the input.

Rule
Split the grid at the vertical midpoint. For each position in one panel,
output pink if the corresponding cell is foreground in either input panel;
otherwise output black.

Key insight
The yellow and green cells are aligned masks, not colors to preserve; the
output is the boolean union of the two masks recolored to a single color.

annotation.src: two side-by-side equal square masks on black background: a yellow mask on the left and a green mask on the right
annotation.transform: overlay the two masks by corresponding positions; output pink where either mask has foreground and black elsewhere
annotation.grid_shape: one-panel canvas, same height and half the input width

references.docstring:
Expand a vertical colored line into a centered alternating-color pyramid.

Input structure:
- The input contains one non-black line segment on a black background.
- The line's dominant column gives the pyramid center column.
- The line length determines the pyramid height and widest row.

Rule:
- Identify the line color, center column, and lowest occupied row.
- Build a black output grid of the same size.
- For each row above the line base, draw a centered run whose colors alternate by distance from the center.

Key insight:
- The original line is the pyramid axis; moving upward shortens the run, while
  horizontal parity controls the alternating colors.

Add blue downward extensions and larger green square frames around each input square.

Input structure:
- The grid contains multiple monochromatic square objects on a black background.
- The square objects may have different sizes but share the same generated color.
- Blue and green are output-only construction colors.

Rule:
- Detect each square object and clear the output background to black.
- Fill blue below each square's original footprint down to the grid bottom.
- Draw a green frame twice the square size around it, then paste the original square back.

Key insight:
- Each square contributes two independent structures: a vertical blue projection from
  its base and a centered doubled-size green frame around the original square.

Connect every horizontally or vertically aligned pair of blue marker pixels with teal segments.

Input structure
- A 2D black-background grid.
- The only foreground pixels are blue markers.
- Some rows and columns contain two or more blue markers.

Rule
- Preserve every input pixel.
- In each row, sort the blue marker columns and paint teal on the background cells strictly between adjacent markers.
- In each column, sort the blue marker rows and paint teal on the background cells strictly between adjacent markers.

Key insight
- The markers are endpoints for straight horizontal and vertical connections; unrelated markers are ignored unless they share the same row or column.

annotation.src: blue marker pixels
annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical segment from each marker to the next blue marker in the same row or column
annotation.trajectory: paint every intervening background pixel teal
annotation.transform: keep the blue markers and unrelated background pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Recover the pattern hidden by the unique solid square occluder using mirror symmetry.

Input structure
- The input is a square scene with one unique largest solid monochrome square occluder.
- The occluder's color appears only in that square, and the rest of the scene is mirror-symmetric.

Rule
- Reflect the occluder's bbox across the vertical axis, horizontal axis, and both axes.
- Ignore reflected regions that still contain the occluder color because they overlap the hidden square.
- Transform each usable reflected region back into the occluder orientation and return that recovered square.

Key insight
- The task asks for only the occluded square, not the full repaired scene; every unoccluded mirror counterpart yields the same patch.

annotation.src: visible mirror-symmetric square-grid pattern outside the unique largest solid square occluder
annotation.dst: region covered by the occluder
annotation.transform: reflect the occluder bbox across the grid's horizontal and vertical axes; from every non-overlapping mirrored region, transform the visible patch back into occluder orientation and output the agreed hidden values
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as the solid square occluder

references.docstring:
Expand each red pixel into a clipped 3x3 blue halo while preserving existing foreground pixels.

Input structure
A black-background grid contains one or more red marker pixels and may contain other non-red foreground markers.
Rule
For every red pixel, recolor each black cell in its Chebyshev-distance-1 neighborhood to blue; do not overwrite any existing foreground pixel.
Key insight
The red pixels are centers of independent 3x3 stamps, clipped by the grid boundary, and the stamp only fills background cells.

annotation.src: red marker pixels on a black background, with optional other foreground markers
annotation.transform: fill every black pixel in each red marker's clipped 3x3 neighborhood with blue; preserve the red markers and all other foreground pixels

references.docstring:
Move the green marker one cell along the straight line toward the yellow marker.

Input structure
- The grid background is the dominant color.
- There is exactly one green marker pixel and exactly one yellow marker pixel.
- The two markers lie on the same row, same column, or a 45-degree diagonal.

Rule
- Keep the yellow marker fixed.
- Clear the original green marker cell to the background color.
- Repaint the green marker one cell closer to the yellow marker along their shared line.

Key insight
- The yellow marker is the fixed destination, and the green marker advances by the normalized row/column direction vector toward it.

annotation.src: single green marker pixel s
annotation.path: one row, column, or 45-degree diagonal step along the straight line from s toward d
annotation.dst: fixed yellow marker pixel d
annotation.trajectory: move only the green marker one cell
annotation.transform: old green cell becomes background; keep the yellow marker and all other background pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor each grey object by the colored top-row marker whose column passes through it.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background, grey rectangular 4-connected objects,
  and colored singleton control pixels in the top row.
- Each grey rectangle has exactly one control-pixel column inside its horizontal span.

Rule
- Keep the background and top-row control pixels unchanged.
- For each 4-connected grey rectangle, find its bounding-box column range.
- Recolor the whole object with the unique control-pixel color whose column
  lies inside that range.

Key insight
- The markers act as vertical labels for grey regions: horizontal-span
  containment, not distance or object size, determines the fill color.

annotation.src: grey rectangular object s
annotation.dst: top-row colored control pixel d
annotation.match_cond: d.col lies within s.bbox.col_span
annotation.transform: recolor all cells of s to d.color

references.docstring:
Return the color of the rectangular region that contains the most rare marker pixels.

Input structure:
- The grid is partitioned into large, mostly solid rectangular color regions.
- One unique rare color appears only as marker pixels embedded inside those regions.
- Each marker's 4-neighborhood identifies the base color of its containing region.

Rule:
- Find the unique least frequent color; these cells are the markers.
- Count how many marker pixels belong to each surrounding region color.
- Output a 1x1 grid containing the unique region color with the largest marker count.

Key insight:
- The markers are not output directly; they vote for the region they sit inside,
  and the winning region's base color is the label to return.

annotation.src: unique least-frequent marker color pixels embedded in mostly solid rectangular color regions
annotation.transform: count markers by surrounding region color and replace the grid with the color of the region containing the most markers
annotation.grid_shape: 1x1 label cell

references.docstring:
Complete straight horizontal and vertical connectors between same-color marker pixels that already share a row or column.

Input structure
- A mostly background grid containing isolated foreground marker pixels of one color.

Rule
- For every row containing at least two original foreground pixels, color the full span from the leftmost to rightmost such pixel.
- For every column containing at least two original foreground pixels, color the full span from the topmost to bottommost such pixel.
- Leave all other cells unchanged.

Key insight
- The markers define all orthogonal line segments by row/column alignment; spans are computed from the input markers, not from newly drawn pixels.

annotation.src: rows and columns containing two or more original foreground marker pixels
annotation.transform: fill the span between the outermost original markers in each such row or column with the marker color; preserve isolated markers and all other background

references.docstring:
Trace a bouncing blue diagonal path upward and recolor the black background teal.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background with exactly one blue pixel.
- The blue pixel is the start of an upward-right diagonal ray.
- The left and right grid edges act as reflection walls.

Rule:
- Starting from the blue pixel, draw blue one step up and horizontally each move.
- Reverse horizontal direction when the next step would leave the grid.
- Stop when the path exits through the top, then change remaining black cells to teal.

Key insight:
- The path behaves like a diagonal ray reflecting only off vertical walls before the
  final background recoloring.

Extend a multicolor cross across the canvas by repeating its color sequences.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one connected multicolor cross on a black background.
- One full row and one full column of the cropped sprite meet at the cross center.
- The row and column colors form the sequences to repeat.

Rule:
- Crop the cross and locate the row and column that pass through its center.
- Copy the input grid as the output canvas.
- Paste the center column and center row sequences repeatedly in both directions.

Key insight:
- The cross is a seed for periodic extension: its central row and column are reused
  at intervals equal to their own lengths.

Restore a noisy striped grid by repainting each stripe line with its dominant color.

Input structure:
- The grid is a full canvas of either horizontal row stripes or vertical column stripes.
- Sparse noise pixels may use stripe colors or extra colors, but each true stripe line
  still has a unique dominant color.

Rule:
- Score the horizontal-stripe interpretation by summing the dominant-color counts of
  every row, and score the vertical-stripe interpretation the same way over columns.
- Choose the uniquely better orientation.
- Repaint each row or column in that orientation entirely with its unique dominant color.

Key insight:
- The correct stripe direction is the one whose lines are much closer to monochrome;
  the output is the clean striped canvas hidden under the noise.

annotation.src: noisy full-grid stripe canvas, with either rows or columns forming the higher-purity stripe lines
annotation.transform: choose the row/column orientation with larger total line-mode support; repaint every selected row or column to its unique dominant color

references.docstring:
Fold the grid across its solid vertical separator, overlaying the reflected right side onto the left side.

Input structure
A non-background vertical separator column spans the full grid height. It
splits the remaining cells into equal-width left and right regions on the
background. Reflected foreground overlaps, when present, have the same color.

Rule
Remove the separator column, mirror the right region horizontally, and
overlay it onto the left region. For each output pixel, keep the foreground
color from whichever folded side is non-background; if both sides are
foreground, their colors must agree.

Key insight
The two sides are complementary halves around the separator, and the output
is the separator-free left-side coordinate system after folding the right
side inward.

annotation.src: two equal-width side regions separated by a solid one-pixel vertical separator column
annotation.transform: remove the separator, mirror the right region horizontally, and overlay non-background pixels onto the left region, requiring same-color agreement on overlaps
annotation.grid_shape: same height as input and width of one side region

references.docstring:
Complete the foreground pattern by rotating it into a square with four-way rotational symmetry.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background and a partial foreground pattern inside one hidden square region.
- The intended square is the unique smallest square containing all foreground pixels whose 90-degree rotation closure has no color conflict.

Rule
- Keep the grid shape and background.
- For each foreground pixel in the inferred square, paint its positions under 0, 90, 180, and 270 degree rotations about the square center.

Key insight
The missing cells are not mirrored; they are exactly the orbit needed to complete quarter-turn rotational symmetry.

annotation.src: foreground pixels inside the unique smallest square whose quarter-turn rotation closure has no color conflict
annotation.dst: missing cells of that same square under 90-degree rotations about its center
annotation.transform: paint each foreground pixel's 0, 90, 180, and 270 degree rotation positions; keep the grid shape and background elsewhere

references.docstring:
Move a colored cross left and downward by the gray counter value.

Input structure:
- The input is a 10x10 black grid with one solid colored row and one solid colored column.
- The row and column share the same non-black, non-gray color.
- The top of the rightmost column contains gray pixels that encode the shift amount.

Rule:
- Count gray pixels in the rightmost column.
- Find the colored cross row, column, and color.
- Recreate the cross on black after moving the row down and the column left by that count.

Key insight:
- The gray pixels are a numeric instruction only; they disappear after determining
  how far to shift the cross.

Stamp the red sprite into every matching empty slot in the gray-and-black pattern.

Input structure
- The grid uses black empty cells, gray support cells, and one red marker sprite.
- The red sprite bbox defines the stamp mask.
- Gray cells inside the sprite bbox define the support signature; if an enclosed interior gray support exists, it is the anchor signature.

Rule
- Scan candidate bbox positions from top-left to bottom-right.
- A candidate matches when every red-mask position is still black and every support-signature position is gray.
- If the sprite bbox has no gray support cells, only border-touching black slots of the same shape match.
- Paint each matched red-mask position red, preserving all other cells.

Key insight
The red cells are a stamp; gray support inside the stamp window, or the grid border for unsupported solid stamps, identifies the blank copies to complete.

annotation.src: red sprite mask s
annotation.dst: black candidate stamp window d in the gray pattern
annotation.match_cond: s.mask cells fit black cells in d; gray support inside s.bbox matches gray cells in d, or solid unsupported s maps to border-touching d
annotation.transform: paint the matched mask cells red; preserve all other cells
annotation.multi_step: scan d top-to-bottom, left-to-right; after each stamp, later d must still have black mask cells

references.docstring:
Recolor each green object according to how many bends its shape contains.

Input structure:
- The grid has several green connected objects on a black background.
- Each object is a small bent shape with one, two, or three corner bends.
- The generated inputs include at least one object for each bend count.

Rule:
- Detect each green object and crop its bounding box.
- Count L-shaped 2x2 bend patterns across all rotations.
- Recolor objects with one, two, and three bends to blue, pink, and red respectively.

Key insight:
- Object color is determined by topology of the mask, not by position or size.

Crop the solid rectangular panel that contains the most red marker pixels.

Input structure
- The grid has one separator/background color whose complement forms multiple
  4-connected solid rectangular panels.
- Each panel is a complete rectangle made from the same visible palette, with
  red and blue marker pixels embedded among teal cells.

Rule
- Count red marker pixels inside each panel.
- Return the exact bounding-box crop of the unique panel with the largest red
  marker count.

Key insight
- The output is already present in the input; the only operation is selecting
  the panel by its red-marker count and cropping it unchanged.

annotation.src: solid rectangular panels on the background, each containing red and blue marker pixels
annotation.transform: select the panel with the largest red marker-pixel count and return it unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop to the selected panel bbox

references.docstring:
Copy complete source-panel sprites onto the opposite marker-only panel by aligning their internal marker pixels.

Input structure
- The input is two equal rectangular panels joined either vertically or horizontally.
- One panel contains complete 4-connected multicolor sprites on its own background.
- The other panel contains only colored marker pixels on a different background.
Rule
- Infer the split and source-target direction for which every target marker
  pixel is covered by exactly one translated source sprite's internal marker mask.
- Stamp each matched source sprite onto the target panel with the source
  background transparent.
Key insight
- The small marker pixels are not output by themselves; their relative
  pattern selects and anchors the complete sprite to copy.

annotation.src: complete 4-connected multicolor sprite s in the source panel
annotation.dst: marker mask d in the opposite panel
annotation.match_cond: s.internal marker colors and relative coordinates equal d up to translation; chosen matches cover every target marker pixel exactly once
annotation.transform: stamp s onto d's panel with s.background transparent; output that panel
annotation.grid_shape: one of the two equal input panels

references.docstring:
Fill hollow gray rectangles with yellow while preserving gray outlines and lines.

Input structure:
- The input has black regions bounded by gray rectangle outlines.
- Gray lines may emanate from rectangle sides.
- The desired fill affects only true hollow rectangle interiors.

Rule:
- Treat gray as the background for separating black interior regions.
- Identify regions whose cropped area is entirely black and whose border is not part of a line.
- Recolor accepted black interiors yellow and paste all regions back over a gray canvas.

Key insight:
- Rectangle interiors are found as black holes inside gray structure, while extra
  gray line contacts are filtered out before filling.

Copy the multicolor template into every solid grey rectangle of matching size.

Input structure:
- A dominant background contains one connected, fully occupied non-grey template.
- One or more solid grey rectangles have the same height and width as the template.

Rule:
- Leave the background and original colored template unchanged.
- Replace each grey rectangle with an exact copy of the template.

Key insight:
- Grey marks blank target regions; the non-grey foreground bbox is the pattern
  that fills every target rectangle.

annotation.src: single fully occupied non-grey template sprite s
annotation.dst: solid grey rectangular target slots d
annotation.match_cond: s.shape == d.shape
annotation.transform: stamp s into every matched d; leave the original template and background unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor each black component according to its size while preserving the grey background.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant non-black background color.
- The only foreground pixels are black.
- Each black 4-connected component has area 1, 2, or 3.

Rule:
- Preserve all background pixels.
- Recolor area-1 black components green, area-2 components red, and area-3 components blue.

Key insight:
- The black cells are not independent pixels; each connected blob is classified by its 4-connected area.

annotation.src: black 4-connected foreground components on a grey background
annotation.transform: preserve the background; recolor each black component by area: size 1 to green, size 2 to red, size 3 to blue

references.docstring:
Repeat a black template object outward in the color and direction of its touching indicator.

Input structure:
- The grid has a non-black background.
- A black template object touches one or more single-pixel indicator objects.
- Each indicator color is different from the background.

Rule:
- Detect the background, template objects, and one-pixel indicators.
- For each touching template-indicator pair, infer the direction from template center to indicator.
- Recolor the template to the indicator color and paste repeated translated copies outward.

Key insight:
- The indicator acts as both a color label and a direction handle for repeated
  translation of the same template shape.

Place a green 3x3 cross centered halfway between two blue pixels.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background with exactly two blue pixels.
- The blue pixels are aligned horizontally or vertically with room between them.
- Their midpoint can hold a centered 3x3 pattern.

Rule:
- Locate the two blue pixels and compute their midpoint.
- Build a 3x3 green plus-sign sprite.
- Paste the sprite centered at the midpoint while preserving the blue pixels.

Key insight:
- The two blue pixels define only the center location; the inserted object is always
  the same green cross pattern.

Remove the solid horizontal divider and overlay the equal-size panels above and below it.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background color.
- A single non-background solid row spans the full width and separates two equal-height panels.
- The separator color does not appear inside either panel, and panel foreground pixels do not collide at the same local coordinate.

Rule:
- Delete the separator row.
- Align the bottom panel over the top panel by local row and column.
- Preserve every non-background pixel from both panels on the merged output canvas.

Key insight:
- The full-width row is not output content; it is a divider telling us to superimpose the two same-size drawings.

annotation.src: two equal-size foreground masks above and below a solid one-pixel separator row
annotation.transform: delete the separator row and overlay the masks by corresponding positions; preserve each source pixel's own color and leave uncovered cells background
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one source mask

references.docstring:
Turn two solid color rows into a two-row checkerboard that alternates the row colors by column.

Input structure:
- The grid has exactly two rows and at least one column.
- Each row is a solid color.
- The two row colors are distinct.

Rule:
- Preserve the top/bottom color order in even-indexed columns.
- Swap the two row colors in odd-indexed columns.

Key insight:
- The input gives the two checkerboard colors and the phase: column 0 keeps the original row order, then every next column flips it.

annotation.src: two solid horizontal bars, one in each row
annotation.transform: replace the same-size two-row canvas with a checkerboard: even columns keep the original top/bottom row colors, odd columns swap them

references.docstring:
Recolor the three gray bars by length rank: longest blue, middle yellow, shortest red.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color, and the only foreground color is gray.
- The gray pixels form exactly three 4-connected straight one-cell-thick bars.
- The three bars have distinct lengths.

Rule
- Preserve the background pixels.
- Recolor the longest bar blue, the middle-length bar yellow, and the shortest bar red.

Key insight
- The bar colors are determined by relative length rank, independent of bar
  position or orientation.

annotation.src: three 4-connected gray one-cell-thick bars on the background, grouped by length
annotation.transform: recolor the longest bar blue, the middle-length bar yellow, and the shortest bar red; preserve background

references.docstring:
Draw black diagonals from the single black pixel across a non-black background.

Input structure:
- The input has one uniform non-black background color.
- Exactly one black pixel sits in the grid.
- The black pixel is the center for four diagonal rays.

Rule:
- Locate the single black pixel.
- Copy the input grid.
- Draw black lines from that pixel in all four diagonal directions to the grid edges.

Key insight:
- The background color is irrelevant after locating the lone black pixel; the output
  is the four diagonal axes through that point.

Stack alternating original and vertically flipped wave patterns into a taller output.

Input structure:
- The input is a colored wave pattern on a black background.
- Wave segments touch in a way that overlaps by one row when repeated.
- The output width matches the input width.

Rule:
- Create an output whose height holds four overlapping copies of the input.
- Flip the input vertically for every other copy.
- Paste original, flipped, original, and flipped patterns with one-row overlaps.

Key insight:
- Alternating vertical flips continues the wave smoothly because each copy starts
  before the previous one fully ends.

Compress nested colored shapes into a small nested-square color summary.

Input structure:
- The input contains nested monochromatic non-black shapes on a black background.
- Outer layers have larger bounding boxes than inner layers.
- Each layer has a distinct color.

Rule:
- Detect the colored objects and sort them from largest bounding box to smallest.
- Create a square output with one ring per detected layer.
- Fill nested squares from outermost to innermost using the corresponding layer colors.

Key insight:
- The output preserves only nesting order and colors; geometric details of the
  original shapes are reduced to one-pixel-thick square layers.

Extend a solid rectangle's color along outward diagonals after they pass through frame corners.
Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, one solid rectangular foreground object, and one one-cell-thick orthogonal frame object in a different color.
Rule
From each outer corner of the solid rectangle, trace the outward diagonal; if the first non-background pixel on that ray is a corner of the frame, continue past that frame pixel and paint every remaining background pixel on the same diagonal with the rectangle color.
Key insight
The frame corner selects which rectangle-corner diagonals are active, and the interior/background part of the ray before the frame is left unchanged.

annotation.src: solid rectangular foreground object s
annotation.path: from each outer corner of s, follow the outward diagonal until the first non-background pixel; the ray is active only if that pixel is an orthogonal corner of the other-color frame, then continues on the same diagonal to the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint only the background pixels beyond the frame corner with s.color
annotation.transform: keep s, the frame, and the interior/background pixels before the frame unchanged

references.docstring:
Extend each control pixel perpendicular to the full bars, marking every bar hit with a 3x3 contact marker.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Exactly one foreground color forms one or more complete parallel rows or complete parallel columns.
- The other foreground color appears as isolated control pixels off those bars.

Rule
- For each control pixel, cast rays in both directions perpendicular to the bars.
- Stop each ray at the first bar cell it reaches and color the control-to-hit segment with the control color.
- After all rays are drawn, stamp a 3x3 block of the bar color centered on each hit, restoring the center to the control color.
- Directions with no bar before the grid edge emit nothing.

Key insight
- The only complete rows or columns identify the bars and their orientation; the contact markers are layered after the rays.

annotation.src: isolated control pixels not on the full bar rows/columns
annotation.path: straight ray in both directions perpendicular to the parallel full bars, stopping at the first bar cell reached in each direction; no ray where no bar is reached
annotation.trajectory: paint the control-to-hit segment with the control color
annotation.transform: after all rays, stamp a 3x3 block of the bar color centered on every hit and restore each center cell to the control color; keep other cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Rotate the entire square grid 90 degrees counterclockwise.

Input structure
The input is a square 2D grid whose cells form a small black-and-one-color
pattern.

Rule
Preserve every cell color and move each cell to its position under a 90-degree
counterclockwise rotation of the whole grid.

Key insight
The foreground shape is not rewritten internally; the complete canvas, including
black cells, is rotated as one pattern.

annotation.src: entire square input grid
annotation.transform: rotate the whole grid 90 degrees counterclockwise, preserving every cell color

references.docstring:
Fill unobstructed horizontal gaps between neighboring foreground objects with maroon.

Input structure
- The grid has one connected background color and one foreground color split into several 4-connected solid rectangles.
- Foreground rectangles can be horizontally separated while overlapping in their row spans.
Rule
- For every pair of foreground rectangles with separated column spans and overlapping row spans, consider the rectangle between their bounding boxes.
- Paint that between-box region maroon when no third foreground rectangle has a bounding box crossing both that horizontal gap and the same shared row span.
- Keep all original pixels unchanged.
Key insight
- The bridges are determined by adjacency of object bounding boxes in horizontal layers, not by scanning each row independently.

annotation.src: black gap regions between horizontally separated 4-connected red rectangular objects
annotation.transform: recolor a gap to maroon across the shared row span of its two red rectangles when no third red bbox crosses both that gap and shared span; preserve all red pixels and other black pixels

references.docstring:
Flow teal pixels across the grid while red edge pixels push the paths aside.

Input structure:
- The black grid has teal pixels on one edge and red pixels on a perpendicular edge.
- Teal starts flow toward the opposite edge.
- Red edge pixels create row or column push effects.

Rule:
- Determine the teal flow direction and red push direction from the occupied edges.
- Start a path from each teal pixel.
- Move along the flow direction, but shift one cell away whenever aligned with any red pixel.

Key insight:
- Red pixels act like directional repellers: they do not move, but their rows or
  columns offset the teal streams.

Extend the inner-color leaf markers into full row and column cuts through the foreground rectangle.

Input structure
- A black background contains one solid rectangular foreground region.
- The rectangle uses exactly two colors: an outer color at all four corners and an inner color mass.
- Single-cell leaf protrusions of the inner color stick into the outer-color margin.

Rule
- A leaf whose only inner-color neighbor is above or below selects its column; a leaf whose neighbor is left or right selects its row.
- Selected rows and columns are recolored to the outer color inside the foreground rectangle.
- The same selected rows and columns are extended through the background outside the rectangle using the inner color.

Key insight
- The protruding leaf pixels are not noise: each is a control marker naming one row or column to cut through the rectangle and continue outward.

annotation.src: single-cell inner-color leaf markers attached to the inner color mass inside the foreground rectangle
annotation.path: a leaf attached vertically selects its column; a leaf attached horizontally selects its row; extend that axis from the rectangle to the canvas edge
annotation.trajectory: paint background cells outside the rectangle on the selected row or column with the inner color
annotation.transform: inside the rectangle, recolor the full selected row or column to the outer corner color

references.docstring:
Crop the foreground shape to its tight bounding box and magnify that crop by a factor of two.

Input structure
A 2D grid with a dominant background color and exactly one non-background color forming a sparse shape.

Rule
Find the tight bounding box of all non-background pixels, crop that rectangular region, and replace each cropped pixel with a 2x2 block of the same color.

Key insight
The output is the entire foreground bounding-box region enlarged, so background gaps inside the shape are scaled along with the colored pixels.

annotation.src: unique non-background foreground mask on a dominant background
annotation.transform: crop to the foreground bbox, then replace each retained pixel by a 2x2 same-color block
annotation.grid_shape: foreground bbox height and width multiplied by 2

references.docstring:
Fill the empty upper half with a vertical mirror of the lower-half pattern.

Input structure
The grid has even height. The upper half is entirely background, and the
lower half contains the foreground pattern to be completed.

Rule
Copy the lower half into the upper half after reversing its row order.
Leave the original lower half unchanged.

Key insight
The blank upper region is the missing reflected counterpart of the visible
lower region.

annotation.src: lower-half foreground pattern below an empty upper half
annotation.dst: empty upper-half region
annotation.transform: fill the upper half with the lower half mirrored vertically; preserve the lower half

references.docstring:
Paint green in each output cell where both side panels are background.

Input structure:
- The grid has a centered solid non-background separator column.
- The separator splits the grid into equal-size left and right panels.
- Each panel is a same-size mask using the shared background and one foreground color.

Rule:
- Remove the separator column.
- Compare the two side panels cell by cell.
- Output background where either panel has foreground, and green where both panels have background.

Key insight:
- The output is the intersection of the two panels' empty space, not a copy of either colored mask.

annotation.src: two equal-size side-panel masks separated by a solid centered vertical bar
annotation.transform: for each corresponding cell, output green iff both side-panel cells are background; otherwise output background
annotation.grid_shape: same size as one side panel

references.docstring:
Expand four diagonal color markers into corner glyphs and add dashed grey sides between them.

Input structure
- The input is a background grid with exactly four foreground pixels.
- The foreground has two colors, each appearing twice, on opposite corners of one
  axis-aligned rectangle.

Rule
- Each marker becomes a centered 3x3 glyph: the center keeps its input color and
  the eight surrounding cells use the other marker color.
- In the open gap between adjacent glyphs on each rectangle side, paint grey dashes.
  A gap cell is grey when its nearest side-end distance is even.

Key insight
- The four pixels are rectangle corners; their diagonal color pairing defines the
  corner glyphs, and the sides are dashed symmetrically inward from both ends.

annotation.src: four colored marker pixels at the corners of an axis-aligned rectangle, with two colors paired on opposite corners
annotation.path: from each corner marker, follow the rectangle side gap toward adjacent corner markers on the same row or column, excluding the cells occupied by the 3x3 corner glyphs
annotation.trajectory: paint grey dashes on side-gap cells whose nearest side-end distance is even
annotation.transform: replace each marker with a centered 3x3 glyph whose center keeps the marker color and whose border uses the other marker color; keep background elsewhere

references.docstring:
Mark background cells in foreground-bearing columns with teal, then repeat the marked grid as a 2x2 tile.

Input structure
- The input is a nonempty 2D grid with one dominant background color.
- Exactly one non-background foreground color appears, and it is not teal.

Rule
- Preserve every original foreground pixel.
- In any column containing at least one foreground pixel, recolor background
  cells to teal.
- Repeat the resulting grid twice vertically and twice horizontally.

Key insight
- The foreground pixels select whole columns of the tile; the output is a
  repeated copy of that completed tile, not a nearest-neighbor scale-up.

annotation.src: entire input grid, with foreground pixels selecting their columns
annotation.dst: 2x2 grid of input-size tile slots
annotation.transform: complete the tile by recoloring background pixels in foreground-bearing columns to teal, then copy that tile into all four slots
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 2

references.docstring:
Use the grey pixels as a mask for the only other input color and turn everything else black.

Input structure
- The grid contains exactly two colors.
- Grey marks the pixels that survive into the output.
- The other input color is the paint color and is not black.

Rule
- Create a black output grid with the same shape as the input.
- Recolor every grey input pixel to the unique non-grey input color.
- Recolor every non-grey input pixel to black.

Key insight
- Grey is not a background here; it is the mask showing where the colored
  shape should appear after the original colored cells are removed.

annotation.src: two-color grid where grey pixels form a mask and the other non-black color is the paint color
annotation.transform: recolor grey mask pixels to the paint color; recolor all original paint-color pixels to black

references.docstring:
Mirror the inner pattern pieces outward across the two red frame halves.

Input structure:
- The grid contains two red frame halves enclosing gray pattern pieces.
- The frame pair may be horizontal or vertical after rotation.
- The inner pattern lies between the red frame halves.

Rule:
- Detect the red frame components and paste them into a blank output.
- Crop the full inner pattern and split it into two halves along the frame axis.
- Mirror each half across its corresponding frame line and paste it outside the frame.

Key insight:
- The red frame halves are symmetry axes; the enclosed gray pattern is split and
  reflected outward rather than copied in place.

Output a vertical list of rectangle colors ordered by frequency after skipping the most common.

Input structure:
- The grid contains separated monochromatic rectangle objects on a black background.
- Rectangles are arranged in an array and colored from several non-black colors.
- Color frequency is measured by object count, not pixel count.

Rule:
- Detect each rectangle object and record its non-black color.
- Sort colors by how many rectangles have that color.
- Drop the most frequent color and write the remaining colors top to bottom in a one-column grid.

Key insight:
- The output is a rank summary of object colors, so rectangle positions and dimensions
  are discarded after counting.

Complete the arithmetic sequence of rectangular side-strokes and turn all remaining background grey.

Input structure
A zero-background 2D grid contains one non-background color. Its 4-connected
objects are clipped rectangular side-strokes: each object occupies the same
set of bbox sides, such as top+right, left+bottom, or a three-sided U.

Rule
Sort the observed stroke bboxes by increasing bbox area. Consecutive bboxes
differ by a constant coordinate delta, so extend that bbox sequence in both
directions until the corresponding clipped side-stroke has no visible pixels.
Paint every visible side-stroke with the input foreground color and paint
all other cells grey.

Key insight
The missing output pixels are not filled from local adjacency; the visible
objects are consecutive members of one larger arithmetic family of rectangular
side-strokes, with larger members clipped by the canvas boundaries.

annotation.src: foreground 4-connected rectangular side-strokes with the same bbox-side pattern
annotation.dst: missing members of the same arithmetic bbox sequence
annotation.transform: sort stroke bboxes by size, extend the constant bbox delta in both directions, clip each generated side-stroke to the grid, paint those pixels with the foreground color, and paint all other cells grey

references.docstring:
Return the three foreground colors as a vertical list ordered by decreasing pixel count.

Input structure
A dominant background contains exactly three foreground color masks.

Rule
Count the pixels of each foreground color, sort the colors from largest mask
to smallest mask, and emit those colors as a 3x1 column.

Key insight
The input positions and mask shapes are distractors; the output is the size
ranking of the color masks.

annotation.src: foreground color masks s ordered by descending pixel count
annotation.dst: rows d of the 3x1 output column from top to bottom
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: emit each mask color as one pixel in its assigned row
annotation.grid_shape: 3x1 column

references.docstring:
Recover the black occluded rectangle from a translationally symmetric pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a repeated color pattern with no true background color.
- A black rectangle masks part of the pattern.
- Non-black cells elsewhere reveal the translational symmetry.

Rule:
- Treat black cells as the occlusion mask.
- Detect translational symmetries while ignoring black.
- Fill each black cell from a non-black cell in its symmetry orbit, then crop the filled rectangle.

Key insight:
- Symmetry orbits provide equivalent unoccluded samples for each missing cell, and
  the answer is only the reconstructed occluded region.

Compress two stacked masks into one mask marking positions empty in both.

Input structure:
- The grid is two same-size square masks stacked vertically.
- Each half contains the same background color plus one distinct foreground color.
- Red is absent from the input and is used as the output marker color.

Rule:
- Compare the two halves cell by cell.
- Output red where both cells are the shared background color.
- Output the shared background color everywhere else.

Key insight:
- The output is the intersection of the background masks, not a transformation
  of either colored foreground object alone.

annotation.src: two same-size square masks stacked vertically, each with one foreground color and the same background color
annotation.transform: for each cell position, write red when both corresponding input cells are background; otherwise write background
annotation.grid_shape: same size as one input half

references.docstring:
Extract the largest rectangular foreground frame and recolor its cropped contents to the marker color.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- There are exactly two foreground colors: one forms complete rectangular
  one-pixel-thick frames, and the other appears as marker pixels/noise.
- The intended frame is the unique largest rectangular frame by bounding-box area.

Rule
- Find the foreground color that forms rectangular frames.
- Crop the bounding box of the unique largest frame of that color.
- In the crop, replace every non-background pixel with the other foreground color.

Key insight
- The marker color supplies the output color; only the largest frame's bbox
  decides which marker pixels are kept and which outside pixels are discarded.

annotation.src: largest complete rectangular frame, including marker-color pixels inside its bounding box
annotation.transform: crop to that frame bbox and recolor every non-background pixel in the crop to the marker color
annotation.grid_shape: bounding box of the largest rectangular frame

references.docstring:
Draw a green marker rectangle below each 2x2 square sized by its color count.

Input structure:
- The input is a 10x10 black grid with separated 2x2 colored squares.
- Each square may contain one to four non-black colors.
- The generated placement leaves room around squares for added markers.

Rule:
- Detect each multicolor square object.
- Count the distinct non-black colors inside it.
- Paste a green rectangle directly below the square with height equal to that count and matching square width.

Key insight:
- The added green shape encodes diversity inside each square: more distinct colors
  produce a taller marker.

Sweep a colored input line diagonally upward-right to form a large square pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a one-cell-wide line containing black and colored pixels.
- Non-black colors appear in the line and determine the output scale.
- The output is a black square canvas.

Rule:
- Set the square size to input line length times the number of distinct non-black colors.
- Place the original line at the bottom-left of the output.
- Repeatedly paste the same line one row up and one column right with clipping.

Key insight:
- Diagonal rays are produced by translating the whole sparse line, so every colored
  input pixel leaves a parallel diagonal trace.

Count red 2x2 squares and mark that count in a fixed blue 3x3 pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a square black grid containing separated 2x2 red squares.
- Up to five red squares may be present.
- The output is always a 3x3 black grid.

Rule:
- Detect all connected red square objects.
- Count how many red squares are present.
- Fill that many positions in the fixed blue order: corners by alternating columns with the center between them.

Key insight:
- The output ignores the locations of the red squares and encodes only their count
  along a predetermined sparse 3x3 sequence.

Recover the hidden 5x5 patch by rotating the scene 180 degrees and cropping the blue-mask location.

Input structure
A scene contains exactly one solid 5x5 blue mask over a larger rotationally symmetric pattern.

Rule
Locate the blue mask, rotate the whole input grid 180 degrees, and return the 5x5 patch at the mask's original bbox.

Key insight
The blue block is an occluder; the hidden pixels are supplied by the opposite 180-degree-corresponding part of the same pattern.

annotation.src: visible 180-degree rotationally symmetric pattern outside the solid 5x5 blue mask
annotation.dst: region covered by the blue mask
annotation.transform: rotate the whole input grid 180 degrees and output the crop at the blue mask bbox
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as the blue mask
